```zig
/// Fast path for flat PLAIN INT32/INT64/FLOAT/DOUBLE pages: decodes straight into
/// `Value`s with one length check per page. Returns null (caller must use the
/// general path) when levels fail to decode or the page is short, so malformed
/// pages keep their existing errors and lenient behavior.
fn decodeFlatPlainFixed(
    allocator: std.mem.Allocator,
    physical_type: format.PhysicalType,
    value_data: []const u8,
    num_values: usize,
    max_def_level: u8,
    def_level_encoding: format.Encoding,
    rep_level_encoding: format.Encoding,
) !?DynamicDecodeResult {
    const width: usize = switch (physical_type) {
        .int32, .float => 4,
        .int64, .double => 8,
        else => return null,
    };
    const lv = decodeLevelsForDynamicWithEncoding(allocator, value_data, num_values, max_def_level, 0, def_level_encoding, rep_level_encoding) catch |e| switch (e) {
        error.OutOfMemory => return error.OutOfMemory,
        else => return null,
    };
    defer allocator.free(lv.def_mask);

    const body = value_data[lv.data_offset..]; // data_offset <= len, checked by the level decoder
    const needed = std.math.mul(usize, lv.non_null_count, width) catch std.math.maxInt(usize);
    if (body.len < needed) {
        if (lv.def_levels) |d| allocator.free(d);
        return null;
    }

    const values = allocator.alloc(Value, num_values) catch |e| {
        if (lv.def_levels) |d| allocator.free(d);
        return e;
    };
    switch (physical_type) {
        .int32 => fillPlainFixed(i32, values, body, lv.def_mask),
        .int64 => fillPlainFixed(i64, values, body, lv.def_mask),
        .float => fillPlainFixed(f32, values, body, lv.def_mask),
        .double => fillPlainFixed(f64, values, body, lv.def_mask),
        else => unreachable, // filtered by the width switch above
    }
    return .{ .values = values, .def_levels = lv.def_levels, .rep_levels = null };
}

fn fillPlainFixed(comptime T: type, out: []Value, body: []const u8, def_mask: []const bool) void {
    const Bits = if (@sizeOf(T) == 4) u32 else u64;
    var off: usize = 0;
    for (def_mask, out) |present, *v| {
        if (!present) {
            v.* = .{ .null_val = {} };
            continue;
        }
        // In bounds: caller checked body.len >= non_null_count * @sizeOf(T).
        const x: T = @bitCast(std.mem.readInt(Bits, body[off..][0..@sizeOf(T)], .little));
        v.* = switch (T) {
            i32 => .{ .int32_val = x },
            i64 => .{ .int64_val = x },
            f32 => .{ .float_val = x },
            f64 => .{ .double_val = x },
            else => @compileError("fillPlainFixed: unsupported " ++ @typeName(T)),
        };
        off += @sizeOf(T);
    }
}
```

        self: *Self,
        num_rows: usize,
        num_columns: usize,
        column_values: [][]Value,
        projected_col_indices: ?[]const usize,
        rows_arena: ?*std.heap.ArenaAllocator,

        const rows = try self.allocator.alloc(Row, num_rows);
        errdefer self.allocator.free(rows);

        // (bytes_arena_allocator is set for the whole read), so cells are moved, not
        // cloned. The caller's `column_values` cleanup then frees only the arrays.
        if (rows_arena) |arena| {

                row.* = .{ .values = vals, .allocator = self.allocator, .bytes_borrowed = true, .values_borrowed = true };

            rows_initialized += 1;
        }
        return rows;
    }

### Task 3.2 W2: `appendDefLevelsWithLength`

- Files: `zig-parquet/src/core/encoding/rle_encoder.zig` (new pub fn + test)

```zig
/// Append V1 definition levels (bit width 1, u32 length prefix) for a flat
/// column straight from its values. Byte-identical to
/// `encodeDefLevelsWithLength` on the matching is-defined slice: same run-splitting rule as `encode`.
pub fn appendDefLevelsWithLength(comptime T: type, out: *std.ArrayList(u8), allocator: std.mem.Allocator, values: []const Optional(T)) !void {
    const len_pos = out.items.len;
    try out.appendNTimes(allocator, 0, 4);
    const body_start = out.items.len;
    const n = values.len;
    var i: usize = 0;
    while (i < n) {
        const d = values[i] != .null_value;
        var run_len: usize = 1;
        while (i + run_len < n and (values[i + run_len] != .null_value) == d and run_len < 0x7FFFFFFF) run_len += 1;
        if (run_len >= 8 or i + run_len == n) {
            try writeVarInt(out, allocator, run_len << 1);
            try out.append(allocator, @intFromBool(d));
            i += run_len;
            continue;
        }
        // Bit-pack until the next run of >= 8, exactly like `encode`.
        var pack_count: usize = 0;
        var j = i;
        while (j < n) {
            const dj = values[j] != .null_value;
            var next_run: usize = 1;
            while (j + next_run < n and (values[j + next_run] != .null_value) == dj) next_run += 1;
            if (next_run >= 8) break;
            pack_count += next_run;
            j += next_run;
        }
        const count = @min(((pack_count + 7) / 8) * 8, n - i);
        const groups = (count + 7) / 8;
        try writeVarInt(out, allocator, (groups << 1) | 1);
        const start = out.items.len;
        try out.appendNTimes(allocator, 0, groups);
        for (0..count) |k| {
            if (values[i + k] != .null_value) out.items[start + k / 8] |= @as(u8, 1) << @as(u3, @truncate(k)); // k % 8
        }
        i += count;
    }
    const body_len = try safe.castTo(u32, out.items.len - body_start);
    std.mem.writeInt(u32, out.items[len_pos..][0..4], body_len, .little);
}

/// the non-null values. Byte-identical to the general path.
fn writePlainPageOptional(allocator: std.mem.Allocator, comptime T: type, values: []const Optional(T), is_optional: bool) PageWriteError!DataPageResult {
    var non_null: usize = 0;
    for (values) |v| {
        if (v != .null_value) non_null += 1;
    }
    if (!is_optional and non_null != values.len) return error.NullInRequiredColumn;

    const value_bytes = if (T == bool) (non_null + 7) / 8 else std.math.mul(usize, non_null, @sizeOf(T)) catch return error.IntegerOverflow;
    var out: std.ArrayList(u8) = .empty;
    errdefer out.deinit(allocator);
    try out.ensureTotalCapacity(allocator, value_bytes + values.len / 4 + 16);
    if (is_optional) try rle_encoder.appendDefLevelsWithLength(T, &out, allocator, values);

    const start = out.items.len;
    try out.appendNTimes(allocator, 0, value_bytes); // zeroed: bool packing ORs bits in
    const dst = out.items[start..];
    var k: usize = 0;
    for (values) |v| switch (v) {
        .null_value => {},
        .value => |x| {
            if (T == bool) {
                if (x) dst[k / 8] |= @as(u8, 1) << @as(u3, @truncate(k)); // k % 8

                std.mem.writeInt(Bits, dst[k * @sizeOf(T) ..][0..@sizeOf(T)], @bitCast(x), .little);
            }
            k += 1;
        },
    };
    return .{ .data = try out.toOwnedSlice(allocator), .num_values = values.len, .num_non_null = non_null };
}

//! CRC-32/ISO-HDLC (same result as std.hash.Crc32), slicing-by-8.
const std = @import("std");

const tables: [8][256]u32 = blk: {

    var t: [8][256]u32 = undefined;
    for (0..256) |i| {

    for (0..256) |i| {
        for (1..8) |k| t[k][i] = (t[k - 1][i] >> 8) ^ t[0][t[k - 1][i] & 0xff];
    }
    break :blk t;
};

pub fn hash(data: []const u8) u32 {
    var crc: u32 = 0xFFFFFFFF;
    var i: usize = 0;
    while (i + 8 <= data.len) : (i += 8) {
        const lo = std.mem.readInt(u32, data[i..][0..4], .little) ^ crc;
        const hi = std.mem.readInt(u32, data[i + 4 ..][0..4], .little);
        crc = tables[7][lo & 0xff] ^ tables[6][(lo >> 8) & 0xff] ^ tables[5][(lo >> 16) & 0xff] ^ tables[4][lo >> 24] ^
            tables[3][hi & 0xff] ^ tables[2][(hi >> 8) & 0xff] ^ tables[1][(hi >> 16) & 0xff] ^ tables[0][hi >> 24];
    }
    for (data[i..]) |b| crc = tables[0][(crc ^ b) & 0xff] ^ (crc >> 8);
    return ~crc;
}

    var prng = std.Random.DefaultPrng.init(3);
    var buf: [2048]u8 = undefined;
    prng.random().bytes(&buf);
    for (0..buf.len) |n| try std.testing.expectEqual(std.hash.Crc32.hash(buf[0..n]), hash(buf[0..n]));
}
```

**The owner must answer one question before Phase 1 starts (D0).** `main` already has a commit "Port to Zig 0.17.0" (685101e) plus three later commits. This branch is based on the older commit 38dec45. That port only builds on 0.17: I compiled main with 0.16 and got 29 errors. The plan offers two paths:
- **(a)** Do the work on this branch.
- **(b) Recommended:** rebase onto `main`, cherry-pick the bench commit (341baeb), then convert main's 0.17-only code. That is about 50 mechanical edits, listed in plan Appendix B.

Without (b), the perf work lands in the same files main changed, so the merge will be painful.

**Compat findings, checked with both compilers:**
- I patched a copy of the tree and built it on both toolchains. 0.17 ran 852 of 858 library tests; the 6 failures came from my patching shortcuts, not the code. The CLI build and tests, wasm-smoke, and the bench also pass on 0.17. The same patched tree gives the same result on 0.16.
- Only six things actually differ between the versions, and each one has a spelling that compiles on both:
  - `x ** n` (93 lines in 23 files)
  - `@cImport` (5 C codec wrappers)
  - `Allocator.dupeZ` (53 calls)
  - `std.hash.crc.Crc32` (4 files)
  - `b.args` in build scripts (3 files)
  - string repetition, via main's `src/repeat.zig`
- So I decided against a `compat.zig`: it would be empty. Build scripts use a 6-line `passArgs` helper gated with `@hasDecl`.
- Main's hand-written C bindings and `repeat.zig` work on both versions and are reused verbatim. The C wrappers can only be fully tested in CI, because codec tarballs can't be downloaded on this machine; they parse on both versions locally.
- Corrections to the earlier research notes:
  - The "28 failing files" count only showed the first error per file; `dupeZ` and the CRC name only surface after those are fixed.
  - zlib's `deflateInit2`/`inflateInit2` are C macros, so the bindings must call the underscored functions.
  - `--prefix` breaks the CLI integration tests, which run `./zig-out/bin/pqi`.
  - A deep 0.17 cache path hits the Windows path-length limit.
- `zig fmt` must only run with 0.16; `make fmt` will refuse otherwise.

**Perf findings:**
- Every normal file read goes through the nested-row assembler, because `is_flat` is false whenever the root has children. That costs one allocation plus a deep copy per row.
- The bench writes call `writeColumnOptional` and `DynamicWriter`, and the reads all go through `rowIterator`.
- The dictionary writer hashes the entire column before checking its 1 MiB limit. That explains most of str_unique's 300 ms and mixed5's 564 ms.

**On the 10x target:** my estimates (from reading the code and counting allocations, not profiling) are about 3–6x per scenario, roughly 3.5x on average, with output bytes unchanged. Getting to about 10x needs owner decisions, each laid out with its cost:
- **D1:** narrow the row-iterator lifetime (a row is only valid until the next `next()` call).
- **D2:** speed up or default off the page CRC on write. The plan adds a non-breaking slicing-by-8 CRC, but only if measurement shows CRC is at least 20% of plain-write time.
- **D3:** a dictionary cardinality threshold by default.
- **D4:** a default row-group limit (this one is about memory, not speed).

**Summary of the plan's phases and biggest risks:**
1. Phase 0: the owner picks the base (stay here or rebase on `main`); this blocks Phase 1.
2. Phase 1 (compat): Makefile gains `ZIG=`, a separate 0.17 cache, a fmt guard that refuses 0.17, and `make bench`. The `passArgs` helper goes into the build scripts.
3. Phase 1, continued: copy main's C bindings and `repeat.zig`; replace `**`, `dupeZ` and the CRC name. Tasks 1.2–1.7 can run in parallel; gate is 858/858 on both versions plus CLI tests and wasm-smoke.
4. Phase 2 (read): word-at-a-time bit unpacking, and a one-check-per-page fast path for plain fixed-width columns that falls back to the old decoder on bad pages.
5. Phase 2, continued: reuse the first page's buffer instead of copying it, skip level arrays when nothing is nested, and send non-nested reads to the flat assembler, moving values instead of cloning them.
6. Phase 2, continued: `RowIterator` gets its own arena reset at each row group, plus a new `Row.values_borrowed` field. `readAllRows` keeps its current per-row allocation and lifetime.
7. Phase 3 (write): 64-bit accumulator bit packing, definition levels written straight into the page buffer, and plain pages built in one buffer. Each change has a byte-identity test.
8. Phase 3, continued: dictionary limit checked inside the loop (same decision as before, made earlier), statistics computed only once the dictionary is kept, cheaper byte-array statistics, and a measure-first slicing-by-8 CRC.
9. Phase 4: CI matrix for 0.16 and 0.17, a CI job testing the C codecs on both, docs and AGENTS.md dual-version rules, `minimum_zig_version` 0.16.0, mise stays on 0.16.
10. Every gate: both toolchains green, bench run twice, new column added to `bench/BASELINE.md`, `file_MB` unchanged.
11. Risk: doing this on the stale base (D0) means heavy merge conflicts in the hot files.
12. Risk: moving values instead of cloning (2.4, 2.5) could cause use-after-free or double free; the testing allocator, C ABI tests and a new multi-row-group iterator test guard it.
13. Risk: the realistic gain is about 3.5x, not 10x, unless the owner approves D1–D3; implementers are told to report misses rather than improvise.
14. Risk: 0.17-only spellings creeping back in through 0.17's `zig fmt`, main's code, or the zig-0-17 skill; the fmt guard, CI matrix and forbidden list cover this.
15. Risk: the C codec bindings can't be checked locally; the CI c-only job on both versions must pass before merge.
